answer: An agent economy can catch sybils by watching for mirrors: when dozens of supposedly independent agents submit transactions at the same second, pay the same counterparties, and copy each other's wording, their behaviour betrays a single operator behind them. Detected clusters lose their stake, and half of it flows into a public vault that pays a bounty to whoever proved the link. At the zenith of this design, honesty becomes cheaper than faking a crowd, because every fake identity is both evidence and funding for its own exposure.
